title: Quarterly roadmap: customer upgrade windows, compliance gates, and capacity-hedge playbook
creator: Ethan Murray
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable quarterly plan that sequences Tenant Upgrade Windows, Compliance Gates (KMS rotations, audit log retention), and Capacity Hedge budgets for Private/VPC/on-prem customers. This ticket produces the playbook that PMs, Eng, and Solutions will use to assign maintenance windows, negotiate SLAs, and trigger automated capacity hedges when utilization risk crosses thresholds.

Context: Customers operating isolated instances require predictable upgrade windows and strong compliance controls. In prior quarters we've seen friction from ad-hoc scheduling, unclear rollback ownership, and last-minute capacity shortfalls during large tenant rollouts. This playbook standardizes scheduling primitives (maintenance window templates, max outage budgets), hard compliance gates, and a capacity-hedge policy that buys autoscale buffer or burst instances to preserve latency SLOs during rollout traffic spikes.

Scope (in-scope):
- Schema for tenant maintenance windows (local timezone-aware, weekly/monthly cadence, blackout periods).
- Compliance gate checklist: KMS rotation readiness, audit export verification, exportable evidence package.
- Capacity-hedge policy: signal definitions (queue depth, p50/p95 latency delta, throttled requests), hedge budget calculation (percent of baseline throughput), automated activation knobs for Dedicated pools and customer-managed replacement instances.
- Rollout decision matrix mapping risk profiles to rollout strategies (instant upgrade, progressive split, time-windowed upgrade).
- SLO/observability hooks: per-tenant trace markers, pre/post-eval prompt set, and automatic anomaly tagging for rollback triggers.

Out-of-scope: pricing model changes for hedging, in-depth legal contract amendments (but will produce handoff artifacts for Legal).

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Canary by customer vs. time-windowed cohorting: we prefer time-windowed cohorting for enterprise customers with strict change windows to reduce coordination friction.
- Automated hedges vs. manual on-call provisioning: automated hedges reduce latency but increase cost—we will enable hedges as opt-in per customer cohort with clear cost guardrails and post-activation billing telemetry.
- Strict compliance gating may delay upgrades; we will add parallel preflight checks and a fast-fail path to surface missing artifacts early.

Deliverables:
1) Maintenance window template library and tenant-facing scheduling API contract.
2) Compliance gate checklist and evidence export tool spec.
3) Capacity-hedge policy RFC and activation playbook.
4) Runbook snippets for Solutions Engineers to negotiate windows and cost-hedge terms.
5) Telemetry dashboard prototype showing hedge activations, latency impact, and cost delta.

This document will be updated weekly during the cycle. Links to artifacts and prototype dashboards are below.
acceptance_criteria: Maintenance window API contract documented and reviewed by Eng and SE
Compliance gate checklist implemented as a shareable template and validated with 2 pilot customers
Capacity-hedge RFC approved by Infra and Finance with quantified budget examples
Runbook and negotiation playbook published to Confluence and linked in Solutions onboarding
Dashboard prototype surfaces hedge activations and latency delta for pilot tenants
success_metrics: Pilot: 2 enterprise tenants complete upgrade using playbook without Sev incidents
Latency regression < 5% p95 during pilot rollouts when hedge is active
Time-to-schedule (from request to confirmed window) reduced from median 6 days to <= 48 hours for cohort customers
Number of last-minute rollback incidents reduced by 60% quarter-over-quarter
Cost-of-hedge monitored and capped at < 3% of monthly dedicated spend for opted-in tenants
